# UWHPC (UW High Performance Computing)

> UWHPC is an official student design team at the University of Waterloo specializing in high-performance computing, parallel programming, and low-level software optimization for computationally intensive workloads.

## Overview

UWHPC pushes the boundaries of software and hardware performance by building distributed systems, CUDA-accelerated engines, and parallel algorithms. Operating under the Sedra Student Design Centre (SDC) at Waterloo, the team serves as an incubator for engineers interested in systems architecture, low-latency execution, and high-performance computing.

## Core Technical Focus

- **Parallel Programming & GPU Computing:** CUDA, OpenMP, MPI, and multi-core CPU optimization.
- **Low-Level Systems & Software Engineering:** Modern C++, memory management, cache-locality profiling, and hardware-software co-design.
- **Distributed Systems:** Scalable multi-node processing architectures and high-throughput execution engines.

## Key Projects & Software

- **Variational Monte Carlo (VMC) Engines:** High-performance parallelized physics simulations built in CUDA C++.
- **XPU Libraries:** Custom math and utility libraries designed for extreme compute efficiency.

## Sponsors & Partners

- **Gold Sponsor:** Jane Street[cite: 1]
- **Institutional Backing:** Sedra Student Design Centre (SDC) at the University of Waterloo.
